security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel code (e.g., capability-aware copyin/copyout, pmap capability validation, or capability register save/restore in context-switch paths) invokes the YBNDRW (Set Bounds Round Down) instruction and an incorrect microarchitectural implementation clears cd.tag when the requested bounds cannot be encoded exactly, despite the rounded-down bounds being strictly within the original capability's authority
security_spec.summary: YBNDRW incorrectly cleared capability tags when bounds couldn't be exactly encoded (copy-paste from YBNDSW), causing FreeBSD kernel to lose valid capabilities that should remain authorized because rounding-down preserves authority

findings.finding: Context-switch path saves/restores only standard GP registers (ra, sp, gp, tp, s0-s11) and FP registers. No CHERI capability registers (PCC, DDC, or capability CSRs) are saved/restored because this FreeBSD kernel tree does not implement RISC-V CHERI capability support. The YBNDRW instruction is never invoked.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(cpu_switch)
        sd      a1, PC_CURTHREAD(tp)
        ld      x13, TD_PCB(a1)
        sd      x13, PC_CURPCB(tp)
        ld      x13, TD_PCB(a0)           /* Save the old context */

findings.finding: Trap entry/exit saves/restores only standard CSRs (sstatus, sepc, stval, scause). No CHERI capability CSRs are handled. This is correct for a non-CHERI kernel, but means the YBNDRW vulnerability pattern cannot manifest here.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(cpu_exception_handler_user)
        save_registers 0
        mv      a0, sp
        call    _C_LABEL(do_trap_user)
        do_ast

findings.finding: Trap handler dispatches standard RISC-V exceptions (page faults, illegal instruction, breakpoint, ecall). No CHERI-specific exception handling (e.g., CHERI tag violations, bounds violations). The illegal-instruction handler delegates to FPE lazy enable, with no YBNDRW or capability instruction decoding.

copyin/copyout performs a simple VM_MAXUSER_ADDRESS range check and byte/word copy with fault handling. No capability-aware bounds checking or YBNDRW invocation. The kernel uses standard integer addresses, not capability-based pointers.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(copyin)
        beqz    a2, copyin_end
        add     a3, a0, a2
        li      a4, VM_MAXUSER_ADDRESS
        bgeu    a3, a4, copyio_fault_nopcb

findings.finding: Boot sequence configures only standard Sv39 page tables and stvec/satp/sstatus. No CHERI CSR initialization (no pcc, ddc, or capability CSRs). No YBNDRW or any CHERI instruction is emitted.
findings.snippet:
va:
        lla     gp, __global_pointer$
        la      t0, cpu_exception_handler
        csrw    stvec, t0
        li      t0, 0
        csrw    sscratch, t0

findings.finding: initriscv performs standard CPU ISA identification via identify_cpu(), SBI init, EFI/DTB memory parsing, and pmap bootstrap. No CHERI capability initialization. No YBNDRW usage.

bhyve VM run loop virtualizes standard CSRs (hgatp, henvcfg, hie, hcounteren, vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, hvip, vsatp). No CHERI capability CSR virtualization. Guest world-switch (vmm_switch.S) saves/restores only GP registers and sstatus/hstatus.

bhyve instruction emulation decodes only standard RISC-V load/store instructions (LB/LH/LW/LD/LBU/LHU/LWU, SB/SH/SW/SD, C.LW/C.LD/C.SW/C.SD). No CHERI capability instructions (YBNDRW, SCBNDR, etc.) are decoded or emulated.
pmap layer implements standard RISC-V page table management (Sv39/Sv48/Sv57). No CHERI capability tag tracking or capability-based memory protection. No YBNDRW or capability bounds manipulation.

CHERI __intcap_t/__uintcap_t type aliases exist for hybrid-compilation compatibility only. On non-CHERI systems, these are aliased to __intptr_t/__uintptr_t. This is compile-time type infrastructure, not runtime YBNDRW invocation.
